excerpt: Although the ASL-2 Standard is appropriate for all of our current models, that may not hold true in the future as our models become more capable.
paraphrase: ASL-2 fits current models but may not remain adequate as capabilities increase.

excerpt: To determine when a model has become sufficiently advanced such that its deployment and security measures should be strengthened, we use the concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards determine when deployment and security measures should strengthen.

excerpt: A Capability Threshold tells us when we need to upgrade our protections, and the corresponding Required Safeguards tell us what standard should apply.
paraphrase: A Capability Threshold signals when protections need upgrading; Required Safeguards specify the applicable standard.

excerpt: A Capability Threshold is a prespecified level of AI capability that, if reached, signals (1) a meaningful increase in the level of risk if the model remains under the existing set of safeguards (2) a corresponding need to upgrade the safeguards to a higher ASL Standard.
paraphrase: A Capability Threshold is a predefined capability level whose attainment signals meaningfully increased risk and the need for higher-level safeguards.

excerpt: In other words, a Capability Threshold serves as a trigger for shifting from an ASL-N Standard to an ASL-N+1 Standard (or, in some cases, moving straight to ASL N+2 or higher).
paraphrase: A Capability Threshold triggers movement from one ASL level to the next, or occasionally to a higher one.

excerpt: Depending on the Capability Threshold, it may not be necessary to upgrade both the Deployment and Security Standards; each Capability Threshold corresponds to specific Required Safeguards that identify which of the ASL Standards must be met.
paraphrase: Not every Capability Threshold requires upgrading both Deployment and Security Standards; each threshold has specific Required Safeguards indicating which standards apply.

excerpt: Below, we specify the Capability Thresholds and their corresponding Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: This section specifies Capability Thresholds and their Required Safeguards.

excerpt: The Required Safeguards for each Capability Threshold are intended to mitigate risk from a model with such capabilities to acceptable levels.
paraphrase: Required Safeguards aim to reduce risk from models at each threshold to acceptable levels.

excerpt: In developing these standards, we have weighed the risks and benefits of frontier model development.
paraphrase: Anthropic weighed risks and benefits of frontier model development in creating these standards.

excerpt: We believe these safeguards are achievable with sufficient investment and advance planning into research and development and would advocate for the industry as a whole to adopt them.
paraphrase: Anthropic believes the safeguards are achievable with sufficient investment and planning, and advocates industry-wide adoption.

excerpt: We will conduct assessments to inform when to implement the Required Safeguards (see Section 4).
paraphrase: Assessments will determine timing for implementing Required Safeguards.

excerpt: The Capability Thresholds summarized below are available in full in Appendix C.
paraphrase: Full detail on the summarized Capability Thresholds is in Appendix C.

excerpt: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) weapons. The ability to significantly help individuals or groups with basic technical backgrounds (e.g., undergraduate STEM degrees) create/obtain and deploy CBRN weapons.
paraphrase: The CBRN Capability Threshold is defined as significantly helping individuals or groups with basic technical backgrounds create/obtain and deploy CBRN weapons.

excerpt: This capability could greatly increase the number of actors who could cause this sort of damage, and there is no clear reason to expect an offsetting improvement in defensive capabilities.
paraphrase: The CBRN capability could greatly expand the pool of actors able to cause harm, without a corresponding defensive improvement.

excerpt: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard and the ASL-3 Security Standard, which protect against misuse and model-weight theft by non-state adversaries, are required.
paraphrase: ASL-3 Deployment and Security Standards, guarding against misuse and non-state weight theft, are required for the CBRN threshold.
